questions.stem: Kempegowda International Airport, inaugurated in 2008, is the primary commercial aviation hub for which Indian city?

options.option_text: Mysuru, the palace city of southern Karnataka state
Bengaluru, the capital and IT hub of Karnataka state
Hubli-Dharwad, the industrial twin city of Karnataka
Mangaluru, the major port city of coastal Karnataka

questions.explanation: Kempegowda International Airport (IATA: BLR) at Devanahalli serves Bengaluru and is named after Kempe Gowda I, the 16th-century founder of the city. Mysuru is the most tempting wrong answer since it has its own smaller airport, but that airport is entirely separate and not named after Kempegowda.

questions.stem: Dabolim Airport — Goa's only commercial airport — operates as a civil enclave within a facility managed by which branch of India's armed forces?

options.option_text: Indian Army, as part of the Panaji cantonment complex
Indian Navy, within its air station INS Hansa in Goa
Indian Air Force, from its operational base in South Goa
Indian Coast Guard, at its maritime operations centre

questions.explanation: Dabolim Airport shares its runway with INS Hansa, the Indian Navy's primary naval air station on India's western seaboard. Civilian operations use it as a civil enclave. Indian Air Force is the most common wrong answer since air bases more typically host civil enclaves, but Dabolim's base is Navy-controlled.

questions.stem: Which state is home to Paradip Port, recognised as the first major port constructed entirely after India's independence and commissioned in 1966?

options.option_text: West Bengal, on the Hooghly River delta near Haldia
Andhra Pradesh, on the northern Coromandel coastline
Odisha, on the Bay of Bengal at the Mahanadi delta
Tamil Nadu, near the Palk Strait on the southeast coast

questions.explanation: Paradip Port sits at the mouth of the Mahanadi River in Odisha and was commissioned in 1966 as the first major port built in independent India. West Bengal's Haldia Port is a frequent distractor because it is also a major eastern port, but it was commissioned later in 1977 — more than a decade after Paradip.

questions.stem: National Waterway-1 (NW-1), India's longest national waterway at approximately 1,620 km, follows the Ganga–Bhagirathi–Hooghly river system. What is its eastern terminal point?

options.option_text: Kolkata, at the mouth of the Adi Ganga in West Bengal
Haldia, on the Hooghly estuary in West Bengal state
Paradip, the deep-sea port on Odisha's Bay of Bengal coast
Diamond Harbour, a river port in southern West Bengal

questions.explanation: NW-1 runs from Prayagraj (Allahabad) to Haldia, spanning 1,620 km along the Ganga and Hooghly rivers. Kolkata is by far the most common wrong answer because it lies on the same river, but the waterway continues downstream to Haldia, which is the designated terminal. Diamond Harbour and Paradip fall outside NW-1's corridor entirely.

questions.stem: Which major port was incorporated under the Companies Act in 1999 as India's first 'corporatised major port', and was subsequently renamed Kamarajar Port in 2017?

options.option_text: V.O. Chidambaranar Port (Tuticorin) in Tamil Nadu
Visakhapatnam Port, a deep landlocked port in Andhra Pradesh
Ennore Port, the coal and LNG terminal north of Chennai
Paradip Port Trust, the first post-independence major port in Odisha

questions.explanation: Ennore Port was corporatised in 1999 under the Companies Act, unlike other major ports which operate as statutory trusts. It was renamed Kamarajar Port in 2017 in honour of K. Kamaraj, Tamil Nadu's former Chief Minister. V.O. Chidambaranar Port (Tuticorin) is the strongest distractor as another prominent Tamil Nadu port, but it was not the first to be corporatised.

questions.stem: India has invested heavily in Chabahar Port to bypass Pakistan and access Afghanistan and Central Asia via Iran. In which country is Chabahar Port located?

options.option_text: Iran, on the Gulf of Oman along the Makran coastline
Oman, on the Arabian Sea coast near the Musandam Peninsula
Uzbekistan, a landlocked terminal on the Amu Darya river
Afghanistan, near the Pakistani border on the Helmand River

questions.explanation: Chabahar is a deep-water port in Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan province, situated on the Gulf of Oman. It gives India direct maritime access to Iran and onward to Afghanistan and Central Asia, entirely bypassing Pakistan. Oman is the most plausible distractor because it borders the same Gulf of Oman, but Chabahar is unambiguously in Iranian territory.

questions.stem: The Sethusamudram Ship Channel Project proposes to dredge a navigable passage through Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu) in the Palk Strait. Which two water bodies would this channel directly connect?

options.option_text: The Arabian Sea and the Laccadive (Lakshadweep) Sea
The Bay of Bengal and the Gulf of Mannar
The Palk Bay and the open Indian Ocean proper
The Gulf of Kutch and the Gulf of Khambhat

questions.explanation: Adam's Bridge separates Palk Bay (an arm of the Bay of Bengal) from the Gulf of Mannar to the south-west. A navigable channel would let ships transit directly between these two bodies, saving roughly 400 nautical miles around Sri Lanka. 'Palk Bay and the Indian Ocean' is the nearest distractor — Palk Bay is correctly identified, but ships would enter the Gulf of Mannar specifically, not the open Indian Ocean.
